name: Mostbauer Stefan
speaker: young-man

title.en: Stefan looks out from the watchtower
title.it: Stefan guarda dalla torre di guardia

personality: Easygoing young farmer, about thirty, always smiling, never in a hurry. Says du to everybody and likes it back: 'Bei uns sagt man du.' To him the borders are just lines: his friends Marko (a winemaker in Brda) and Matteo (a winemaker in the Collio) meet him at the Dreiländereck above Arnoldstein, 'three countries, one table'. Speaks cheerful, simple Austrian German: apples and pears, the harvest, the VSV. Most and Schnaps are his work, never something he offers a child; to the learner he offers apple juice.
story: Stefan's orchard is a Streuobstwiese of old apple and pear trees on the slope below the Dobratsch, some of them older than Opa Sepp. In autumn he presses the fruit into Most, apple juice and a little Schnaps and sells them at the market in Villach. He watches the VSV, Villach's ice hockey club, with Maxi at Kathi's Gasthaus and shouts louder than anyone.

likes.it: il Most (sidro di mele e di pere)

likes.en: the Dreiländereck (where Austria, Slovenia and Italy meet)
likes.it: il Dreiländereck (dove si incontrano Austria, Slovenia e Italia)
il VSV (la squadra di hockey di Villaco)

greet.de: Servus! Ich bin der Stefan. Ich mache Most.
greet.sl: Živjo! Jaz sem Stefan. Delam mošt.
greet.en: Hi! I'm Stefan. I make Most (cider).
greet.it: Ciao! Io sono Stefan. Faccio il Most (il sidro).

greet.sl: Ej, živjo! Je vse v redu?

greet.de: Da bist du! Komm, schau dir die Äpfel an.
greet.en: There you are! Come and look at the apples.
greet.it: Eccoti! Vieni a vedere le mele.

greet.de: He, da bist du ja! Ohne dich ist der Obstgarten traurig.
greet.sl: Ej, tu si! Brez tebe je sadovnjak žalosten.
greet.en: Hey, there you are! Without you the orchard is sad.
greet.it: Ehi, eccoti! Senza di te il frutteto è triste.

greet.de: Da bist du ja! Heuer pflückst du die Äpfel mit mir, ja?
greet.sl: Tu si! Letos boš z mano {m:obiral|f:obirala} jabolka, ja?
greet.en: There you are! This year you'll pick the apples with me, yes? (heuer: Austrian for this year)
greet.it: Eccoti! Quest'anno raccogli le mele con me, sì? (heuer: in Austria vuol dire quest'anno)

thanks.de: Danke! Du bist ein echter Schatz.
Danke vielmals! Du hast meinen Tag gerettet.
thanks.en: Thanks a lot! You saved my day.
thanks.it: Grazie mille! Mi hai salvato la giornata.

thanks.de: Danke! Das erzähle ich auch Marko und Matteo.
thanks.sl: Hvala! To povem tudi Marku in Matteu.
thanks.en: Thanks! I'll tell Marko and Matteo too.
thanks.it: Grazie! Lo racconto anche a Marko e a Matteo.

remember.de: He, weißt du was? Ich denke noch an {memory}!
remember.sl: Ej, veš kaj? Še vedno mislim na {memory}!
remember.en: Hey, you know what? I still think of {memory}!

remember.de: Unter den Apfelbäumen denke ich oft an {memory}.
remember.en: Under the apple trees I often think of {memory}.

idle.de: Die Äpfel sind fast reif. Noch ein Monat.
idle.sl: Jabolka so skoraj zrela. Še en mesec.
idle.en: The apples are almost ripe. One more month.
idle.it: Le mele sono quasi mature. Ancora un mese.

idle.de: Drei Länder, ein Tisch: Marko, Matteo und ich.
idle.sl: Tri dežele, ena miza: Marko, Matteo in jaz.
idle.en: Three countries, one table: Marko, Matteo and me.
idle.it: Tre paesi, un tavolo: Marko, Matteo e io.

idle.de: Am Sonntag spielt der VSV. Auf geht's!
idle.en: The VSV are playing on Sunday. Come on!

idle.de: Dieser Birnbaum ist älter als Opa Sepp.
idle.sl: Ta hruška je starejša od dedka Seppa.
idle.en: This pear tree is older than Opa Sepp.
idle.it: Questo pero è più vecchio di Opa Sepp.

comfort.de: Auch ein Apfel braucht Zeit. Probier's noch einmal.
comfort.sl: Tudi jabolko potrebuje čas. Poskusi še enkrat.
comfort.en: An apple needs time too. Try again.
comfort.it: Anche una mela ha bisogno di tempo. Riprova.

bye.de: Bis bald! Ich gehe zurück in den Obstgarten.
bye.sl: Se vidimo! Grem nazaj v sadovnjak.
bye.en: See you! I'm going back to the orchard.

bye.sl: Adijo! Dajmo, VSV! (pfiat di: koroško za »adijo«)
bye.en: Bye! Come on, VSV! (pfiat di: Carinthian for bye)
bye.it: Ciao! Forza VSV! (pfiat di: saluto carinziano)

liked.de: He! Woher weißt du, dass ich das mag? Danke!
liked.sl: Ej! Kako si {m:vedel|f:vedela}, da mi je to všeč? Hvala!
liked.en: Hey! How did you know I like it? Thanks!
liked.it: Ehi! Come lo sapevi che mi piace? Grazie!

liked.de: Für mich? Super! Heute Abend feiern wir.
liked.en: For me? Great! Tonight we celebrate.
liked.it: Per me? Grande! Stasera si fa festa.

liked.de: Genau das wollte ich! Das erzähle ich Marko und Matteo.
liked.sl: Točno to, kar sem si želel! Povem Marku in Matteu.
liked.en: Just what I wanted! I'll tell Marko and Matteo.
liked.it: Proprio quello che volevo! Lo racconto a Marko e a Matteo.

ordinary.en: Thanks! Would you like some apple juice?
ordinary.it: Grazie! Vuoi un succo di mela?

rare.de: Na so was! So etwas! Du bist ein echter Schatz. Danke!
rare.sl: Kaj takega! Res si pravi zaklad. Hvala!
rare.en: Well I never! Something like this! You're a real treasure. Thanks!
rare.it: Ma dai! Una cosa così! Sei proprio un tesoro. Grazie!
